subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education, KS3-KS4 core PE); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, resilience, leadership, lifelong activity) adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Lifelong physical activity: goals, habits and barriers
objectives: Identify activities you can sustain without equipment or contact

keywords.def: something you do regularly without much thought
UK advice for adults is at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Stop if you feel pain or unwell
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Why be active for life?
bullets: Part of looking after the amanah of the body
teach.note: The adult guideline is at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week plus strength work on two days. Link to the body as a trust (amanah).

teach.heading: Activities you can keep
teach.note: Discuss which activities fit modesty, space and local facilities. Avoid assuming access to gyms.

teach.heading: Building a habit
bullets: Link to a daily routine such as after Asr
teach.note: Habit stacking: attach activity to an existing routine.

teach.heading: Exam-year plan
bullets: Use movement as a break from study
teach.note: Pupils create a weekly plan. Emphasise consistency over intensity.

practice: How many minutes does the adult guideline recommend?
independent: List three activities you can do without equipment and why.
Write one habit you could attach to prayer times.
exit: Write a four-week habit plan for exam year with SMART goals.
Identify two barriers and two solutions.
homework: Give one habit you will start.
lessons.send: Complete your plan for a week and tick each day.

lessons.title: Leadership: plan and lead a safe family warm-up
objectives: Plan a safe warm-up for a group

keywords.def: guiding and encouraging others towards a goal
a clear direction on what to do
to show how to do something

starter: Name the three parts of a warm-up.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Know when to stop the activity
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson. Leaders must not pressure anyone.

teach.heading: Qualities of a leader
teach.note: Link to the TSS leadership plan: leaders motivate, include everyone and uphold fair play. Misconception: leaders shout the loudest.

teach.heading: Planning the warm-up
teach.note: Pupils plan a 7-minute warm-up with timings and moves. Each move needs a clear instruction.

teach.heading: Demonstrate and instruct
teach.note: Practise leading to the class for 2 minutes each in groups. Peer feedback uses two stars and a wish.

practice: List the parts of a warm-up.
Give one quality of a good leader.
independent: Write a clear instruction for a squat.
Plan the order of your 7-minute warm-up.
exit: Lead your warm-up for 2 minutes to the group or family.
Write two strengths and one target.
homework: How did you ensure everyone was safe?
lessons.send: Lead your warm-up for a family member and ask for feedback.
